summary: **In the matter of:** Petition, under Section 79 of the Electricity Act, 2003 read with Article 13 of the Power Purchase Agreement dated 22.04.2007 and Clause 4.7 of the Competitive Bidding Guidelines and this Hon’ble Commission’s Order dated 17.09.2018 in Petition No. 77/MP/2016. _15. In these facts and circumstances of the case, we find it appropriate to remand the case back to the Commission for a fresh consideration on the above noted submissions/contentions raised on behalf of the Appellant._ _16. Hence, the impugned order is hereby set aside to the extent it has been assailed in this Appeal. The appeal stands allowed. The case is remanded back to the Commission for fresh consideration on the aspect noted herein above after hearing the parties again. Needless to say that the Commission shall complete the exercise expeditiously and not later than three months from the date of the receipt of this order from this Tribunal.”_ - _“ ..The Petitioner was directed to submit on an affidavit within two weeks, the following information along with the supporting documents in regards to Issue No. 3 as dealt with by the Commission vide order dated 22.6.2020 in Petition No. 168/MP/2019:_ 6. The Petitioner, vide its affidavit dated 19.7.2024, submitted the information as directed by the Commission in the RoP dated 18.6.2024 and mainly submitted as below: 8. The Petitioner, vide its affidavit dated 9.10.2024, submitted a rejoinder to Respondent No.1, GUVNL’s reply dated 16.8.2024, and mainly submitted as below: 9. The counsel for Respondent Nos. 3-8 requested permission to file their respective replies in the matter. In response, the Commission granted all Respondents three weeks to submit their replies, with a copy provided to the Petitioner, who may file rejoinders within three weeks thereafter. 11. The reply on behalf of Respondent Nos. 3 to 5, the Rajasthan utilities, was filed through an affidavit dated 13.10.2024 in response to the additional affidavit dated 19.7.2024 filed by the Petitioner. In their submission, the Rajasthan utilities reiterated the same contentions as raised by Respondent Nos. 7 and 8. Similarly, Respondent No. 6, Punjab State Power Corporation Limited (PSPCL), filed a reply vide its affidavit dated 11.10.2024 to the additional affidavit dated 19.7.2024 filed by the Petitioner, also reiterated the contentions raised by Respondent Nos. 7 and 8. In response, the Petitioner filed a rejoinder, vide its affidavit dated 16.11.2024, addressing the replies from Haryana, Rajasthan, and Punjab procurers, and reiterating the facts previously stated in their submissions. 12. The matter was heard virtually. The learned senior counsel for the Petitioner began arguments by referring to a Note of Arguments but requested a physical hearing due to the technical complexity of the matter. The Respondents did not oppose this suggestion, although the counsels for PSPCL and HPPC requested that the Petitioner be directed to share the Note. The Commission agreed and directed the Petitioner to provide a copy of the Note of Arguments to the Respondents. 13. During the hearing, the senior counsel for the Petitioner and the counsels for the Respondents presented their arguments regarding whether the Petitioner is entitled to claim capital and operational expenditure (Capex and Opex) for the FGD system based on the full installed capacity of 4,150 MW or the 4,000 MW considered earlier. After hearing both sides, the Commission directed the Petitioner to submit its written submissions within two weeks, with the Respondents given two weeks thereafter to file their responses. The matter was then reserved for order. 15. Aggrieved by the above Commission’s findings, the Petitioner filed a Review Petition (No. 30/RP/2020), which was dismissed on 16.08.2021. Subsequently, on 04.10.2021, the Petitioner filed Appeal No. 240 of 2022 to the Hon’ble Appellate Tribunal for Electricity, challenging the Commission’s Order dated 22.06.2020, particularly its conclusion that Procurers are liable to pay capital and operational costs on a pro-rata basis for 4,000 MW, while TPCL’s costs are considered for 4,150 MW. On 14.05.2024, the Hon’ble Appellate Tribunal set aside the Commission’s Order to the extent challenged and remitted the matter back for fresh consideration. The relevant extract of the Hon’ble APTEL’s Order dated 14.05.2024 in Appeal No. 240 of 2022 is as under: _15. In these facts and circumstances of the case, we find it appropriate to remand the case back to the Commission for a fresh consideration on the above noted submissions/contentions raised on behalf of the Appellant._ _16. Hence, the impugned order is hereby set aside to the extent it has been assailed in this Appeal. The appeal stands allowed. The case is remanded back to the Commission for fresh consideration on the aspect noted herein above after hearing the parties again. Needless to say that the Commission shall complete the exercise expeditiously and not later than three months from the date of the receipt of this order from this Tribunal.”_ 16. On perusal of the above Hon’ble APTEL’s Order dated 14.05.2024 in Appeal No. 240 of 2022, the following conclusion can be drawn from the order: contentions raised by the Appellant. Accordingly, the Hon’ble Tribunal set aside the impugned order to the extent it was assailed in the present Appeal and remanded the case back to the Commission for reconsideration of the above aspects. - d. That the Hon’ble Tribunal further directed the Commission to undertake the necessary assessment after affording both parties an opportunity of hearing and to complete the exercise expeditiously, preferably within a period of three months from the date of receipt of the order. 21. In view of the above, the Commission agrees with the Petitioner that the capacity 24. With this order, the directions of APTEL in Appeal No. 240 of 2022 stand implemented, and the Petition stands disposed of to the extent of the remand.
